subject: merge-sort

composition.story: Start with Input [4, 1, 3, 2]. Split into Left and Right, then single values. Merge those into sorted halves. Compare their fronts: Right’s 2 goes before Left’s 4. Repeating this rule builds sorted Output [1, 2, 3, 4]. Use Next and Previous to inspect each state.

aha.observation: Merging sorted groups requires comparing only their front values, because each front is its group’s smallest remaining value.

parts.presentation: Use the approved card shell and canonical algorithm/collection composition. Place story and instructions above the experiment. Keep progress on this rail. Parameter-control budget: zero, excluding navigation and Reset.

Show only the active snapshot as one highlighted row; inactive snapshots remain hidden. Preserve group order and readable label space. Group labels name Input, Left, Right, and Output; brackets delimit groups. Empty brackets mean exhausted groups. Assume ascending numerical order with this fixed, distinct-integer input. Use no animation.
Anchor to the active row without covering values. Identify the relevant group in words; do not repeat numerical values.

controls.label: Sorting step
controls.presentation: Use Previous and Next buttons. Default to the first state; bounds are the first and last states; increment by one state. Retain button names when disabled at boundaries. Every state persists until learner action, including compare-fronts. Reference captures show compare-fronts. Provide visible focus, keyboard activation, and Left/Right arrow navigation. states.label: Unsorted input
states.why: Merge sort first splits the input, then merges sorted groups.

states.label: Split into halves
states.sentence: Split Input into Left and Right without rearranging their values.
states.why: Each half becomes a smaller sorting problem.

states.label: Split to single values
states.sentence: Split Left and Right again into single-value groups.
states.why: Every single-value group is already sorted.

states.label: Merge within each half
states.sentence: Merge each adjacent pair of single-value groups, taking the smaller front first.
states.why: Left and Right are now sorted groups, ready for the final merge into Output.

states.label: Compare the remaining fronts
states.sentence: Left’s first value has entered Output; Right now has the smaller front.
states.why: Each group is sorted, so only their front values can be next.

states.label: Take Right’s smaller front
states.sentence: Append Right’s smaller front to Output, leaving Left unchanged.
states.why: Choosing the smaller front keeps Output sorted.

states.label: Repeat the comparison
states.sentence: Right again has the smaller front; append it to Output.
states.why: Right is now empty, so Left’s remaining values can be appended directly.

states.label: Finish the merge
states.sentence: Append Left’s remaining value to complete Output.
states.why: Repeatedly taking the smaller front has combined the sorted halves into one sorted result.
